name: Veyran, Voice of Duality
oracle_text:
Magecraft — Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell, Veyran gets +1/+1 until end of turn.
If you casting or copying an instant or sorcery spell causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time.
blocked_sentences: Magecraft — Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell, Veyran gets +1/+1 until end of turn.
If you casting or copying an instant or sorcery spell causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time.

needs.what: a trigger event that fires when you copy an instant or sorcery spell -- a `spell_copied` event (or an equivalent `copied: true` / `include_copies: true` filter key on `spell_cast`) that fires once per copy created, whether the copy is put onto the stack without being cast or is cast. It must carry the same filter surface `spell_cast` has (`controller: "you"`, `types: ["Instant", "Sorcery"]`) so the two halves of magecraft can be written as one trigger or as two identically-filtered triggers claiming the same printed line, and its firing rules must be pinned deliberately for a copy that is also cast (707.10/608.2: the printed wording fires magecraft once for the cast and once for the copy). Veyran's effect half needs nothing new -- it is `pump` with `power: 1`, `toughness: 1`, `duration: "end_of_turn"` on `{"self_only": true}` -- so this event is the only thing standing between the card and an answer. Same requirement as Archmage Emeritus (draw a card) and Storm-Kiln Artist (create a Treasure); building the event once clears all three effect bodies at once.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `trigger_events` contains `spell_cast`, which covers only the cast half; nothing in the list observes a copy being created. `copy_spell` and `cast_copy` are in `ops` -- effects that *make* a copy, not events that *notice* one, so they cannot hear another card's copying. `condition_keys` has `was_cast`, but a condition can only narrow a trigger that already fired, and it is false for a copy that was never cast. Writing this as a bare `spell_cast` trigger would ship a strictly weaker Veyran that silently misses every copy -- and Veyran is a copy-deck commander, so the missing half is the half the card exists for.

needs.what: the same `double_triggers` static effect Harmonic Prodigy needs, but scoped along a DIFFERENT axis, so the capability must support both shapes rather than one. Harmonic Prodigy scopes by the SUBTYPE OF THE PERMANENT that owns the triggered ability ("a Shaman or another Wizard you control") -- a `static_filter_keys` filter over the permanent. Veyran scopes by the CAUSE OF THE TRIGGER: the permanent may be any permanent you control, but the doubling applies only when the event that caused the ability to trigger was YOU CASTING OR COPYING an instant or sorcery spell. So the effect needs, beside its permanent filter, a `cause` clause naming the triggering event -- something like `{"cause": {"kind": "spell_cast_or_copied", "controller": "you", "types": ["Instant", "Sorcery"]}}` -- which means the trigger-queueing path has to carry a reference to the event that queued each ability, not just the ability and its source. Concretely: Veyran doubles a permanent's "whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell" trigger and its own magecraft trigger, but does NOT double that same permanent's enters, dies, upkeep or attack triggers; Harmonic Prodigy doubles every triggered ability of a matching creature regardless of what caused it. Both also share the general requirements: each extra instance is independent (targets and modes chosen separately as it goes on the stack), it applies to triggered abilities of permanents only, and multiple such effects compound per the controller's ordering of replacement effects (CR 614.1b). Note the `cause` clause depends on the `magecraft` gap above -- "copying" is not an observable event today -- so this shape cannot be tested until a copy event exists.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `static_effects` has exactly one trigger-doubling entry, `double_land_triggers`, and it is hard-scoped to land-enters triggers: it cannot see a spell-cast trigger, carries no filter for which permanents it covers, and has no notion of the causing event at all. It doubles by one fixed event type, which is the wrong axis for both Harmonic Prodigy (permanent subtype) and Veyran (causing event). Nothing in `ops` substitutes: `reflexive_trigger` and `delayed_trigger` create new one-shot triggers from a resolving effect, and `copy_spell`/`cast_copy` copy stack objects from a resolving effect -- none is a continuous static that intercepts another permanent's ability as it triggers. `condition_keys` cannot help either: it can gate an ability Veyran itself has, not intercept somebody else's. Authoring Veyran with an unscoped doubler would double every trigger of every permanent you control and make the card silently far stronger than printed; authoring it with Harmonic Prodigy's subtype filter would double the wrong things entirely.
